reasoning_details.summary:
**Formulating test approaches**

I’m thinking about combining tests, but I don’t believe the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) needs to be extensive. There’s an assumption that we shouldn’t mention external broker environments and I need to avoid claiming unsupported implementation details. I see that the U5 domain ideas might be captured in documentation, while U8 would focus on proof-of-concept implementation. It’s key that activities have IDs, and decisions are organized as array strings in JSON format. Let’s put this together!

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the increment within the existing Spring XD command, REST, stream-deployment, module, and message-bus abstractions rather than introducing a new management subsystem.
Associate provisioned queues, topics, channels, and other bus resources with stream and module metadata so cleanup can be performed deterministically.
Make resource cleanup idempotent and tolerant of already-deleted or unavailable resources, while reporting cleanup failures clearly.
Implement stream editing as an update of stream definition and deployment properties, using a controlled undeploy/redeploy or rolling update strategy supported by the existing platform.
Support deployment manifests as file-based input through the existing command-line deployment workflow, with validation before resources are changed.

Represent trace configuration as deployment properties supporting explicit module names and wildcard module patterns, and implement tracing using Spring Integration wiretaps or the equivalent existing channel interception mechanism.
Represent optional side channels as module-level channel definitions that are provisioned and bound independently from the primary stream input and output channels.
Deliver the reference architectures as documented Spring XD examples and capture raw domain-specific ideas rather than attempting to build production-grade solutions.
Deliver the taxi-trip work as a runnable demonstration pipeline with documented data assumptions, replay or ingestion support, and representative real-time analytics.
assumptions: The work is based on an existing Spring XD codebase with established build, test, command-line, deployment, module, metadata, and message-bus provider abstractions.
The increment includes all eight user stories, including implementation, documentation, examples, and tests.
Existing supported message-bus providers expose sufficient APIs for queue/topic creation, lookup, and deletion; no new broker provider is required.
Stream and deployment metadata can be extended without a database migration that affects unrelated installations.
Backward compatibility with existing stream creation and deployment commands is required.
The manifest format will use the repository's existing configuration convention, assumed to be YAML or properties, rather than introducing a new custom format.
Trace and side-channel behavior is limited to stream deployment and module channel configuration; no new distributed tracing backend or notification service is required.
The taxi-trip demonstration uses an available public or representative sample of the DEBS 2015 New York City taxi-trip data and does not require production-scale performance certification.
Reference architectures require design documentation, diagrams or configuration examples, and minimal runnable examples where practical, not complete enterprise applications.

Effort includes developer-level testing, integration testing against a representative message broker, documentation, and regression fixes, but excludes project management, release operations, and long-term maintenance.
One workday represents one person-day of productive development effort; estimates are effort estimates rather than elapsed calendar duration.

activities.activity_description: Analyze the eight user stories, inspect existing Spring XD stream and deployment behavior, define interactions among cleanup, editing, manifests, tracing, and side channels, and produce implementation-level designs and acceptance scenarios.
Set up or update the local development environment, identify affected modules and extension points, verify build and test baselines, and prepare representative broker and deployment configurations.

Implement ownership tracking and deletion of queues/topics and related message-bus resources when streams are destroyed, including stale-resource discovery, cleanup commands or hooks, idempotency, error handling, and support for U1 and U2.

Implement stream definition and deployment-property editing, validation, persistence, command or API support, and the required update lifecycle for both deployed and undeployed streams without requiring explicit destruction.
Add file-based deployment manifest input, parsing, validation, property merging and precedence rules, useful command-line diagnostics, and compatibility with existing inline deployment properties.

Implement explicit and wildcard trace properties such as module-specific and module-wide patterns, connect them to Spring Integration wiretap or equivalent channel interception behavior, and expose configuration and error handling through stream deployment.

Design and implement module-level declarations for additional channels, provision and bind those channels on the message bus, expose them to downstream tracing or tracking consumers, and preserve primary stream channel behavior.

Capture domain-specific reference ideas, select representative architectures, create stream/module configurations and explanatory documentation, and provide minimal examples suitable for proof-of-concept development.

Create the taxi-trip ingestion or replay flow, parsing and transformation components or configurations, representative real-time analytics, operational instructions, sample data handling, and demonstration documentation for U8.

Add tests for lifecycle cleanup, stale-resource handling, stream editing, manifest parsing, trace matching, side channels, examples, and failure cases; execute integration tests with a representative broker and validate cross-feature behavior.
Document commands, manifest syntax, cleanup behavior, editing semantics, trace and side-channel properties, migration or compatibility notes, reference architectures, and the taxi-trip demonstration.
Review the complete increment, resolve integration and compatibility defects, run the full regression suite, verify clean-install and upgrade scenarios, and prepare the implementation for delivery.
